I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for thirty years. My body knows the calendar — wheat goes in October, maize follows after the June harvest. All 9 mu rotates between the two. That's just how it's done here, and it's worked.

My son and daughter-in-law are in Baoding most of the year. It's mostly me and my husband working the fields, with help from neighbors during sowing and harvest. I hire a rotary tiller machine — I can't manage deep tillage by hand anymore, and everyone on the village does the same.

For **wheat**: I'll buy Kenong 199 seeds from the county seed shop, same as last year. It yields well and handles the cold. After the maize straw gets chopped and rotary-tilled in October, I'll sow. I water four times — before sowing, again before the ground freezes in December, then at jointing in April, and once more at heading. My well goes down some years, but it's held. I apply diammonium phosphate as base fertilizer before sowing, then top-dress with urea at jointing. I spray herbicide in spring and do one fungicide pass when the flag leaf comes out. I expect around 450 jin per mu — a good year gets me 500.

For **maize**: I plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June, no time to waste. I use Xianyu 335 hybrid seed — neighbors switched to it years back and I followed. I rotary-till lightly after the wheat straw is cleared. Maize gets less fertilizer at planting, then a heavy urea top-dress at the big bell stage. Rain usually helps in July and August, but I water twice — once at emergence if it's dry, once at silking. I spray for corn borer once, herbicide once early on. I expect 550–600 jin per mu.

I don't change much year to year. What I know works, I keep doing.
